tan² A = sec² A - 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ sec2 A - 1 + 5 sec A - 13 = 0

∠ABC = 58° and ∠ACB = 34°

A bisector of an angle divides the angles into equal parts

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AC and BD are two chords. AC and BD meet at E, when produced. If AB is a diameter and ∠AEB = 36°, then the measure of ∠DOC is:

**Given:**

∠AEB = 36°

**Concept used:**

The sum of all angles on a straight line = 180°

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1f9815a72b520b1c67be037014a1229878996455c02e16a9112b92fe230d2dd.png] **

Suppose, AC = BD

Then, ∠CAO = ∠ACO = ∠OBD = ∠ODB

So, ∠CAO = ∠ACO = ∠OBD = ∠ODB = (180° - 36°)/2 = 72°

∴ ∠AOC = ∠BOD = 180° - (2 × 72°) = 180° - 144° = 36°

So, ∠DOC = 180° - ∠AOC - ∠BOD

= 180° - 36° - 36° = 108°

**∴ The measure of ∠DOC is 108°**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method:__**

Let ∠A = a and ∠B = 144∘ - a

Now in ΔOAC and ΔOBD,

∠OAC = ∠OCA and ∠OBD = ∠ODB

∴ ∠AOC = 180∘ - 2a

∠BOD = 2a - 108∘ 

 ⇒ ∠AOC + ∠BOD + ∠DOC = 180∘

⇒ 180∘ - 2a + 2a - 108∘ + ∠DOC = 180∘ 

⇒ ∠DOC = 108∘

questions.question: Five men and 2 boys can do in 30 days as much work as 7 men and 10 boys can do in 15 days. How many boys should join 40 men to do the same work in 4 days?
questions.solution:
Given:

5 men and 2 boys can do a work in 30 days

7 men and 10 boys can do the same work in 15 days

Concept used:

Time = Work/Efficiency

Calculation:

Let, M = Men; B = Boys

(5M + 2B) × 30 = (7M + 10B) × 15

⇒ 150M + 60B = 105M + 150B

⇒ 150M - 105M = 150B - 60B

⇒ 45M = 90B

⇒ M/B = 90/45 = 2/1

So, the efficiency of one man = 2

Efficiency of one boy = 1

Total work = [(5 × 2) + (2 × 1)] × 30 = 12 × 30 = 360

Efficiency of 40 men = 40 × 2 = 80

Time required to finish work = 4 days

Now, 360/(80 + B) = 4

⇒ 90 = 80 + B

⇒ B = 90 - 80 = 10

**∴ The total number of 10 boys should join to do the work**

questions.question: If 8A5146B is divisible by 88, then what is the value of BA?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The given number = 8A5146B

**Concept used:**

**Divisibility rule of 8:** If the last three digits of a number is divisible by 8, the number will be divisible by 8

**Divisibility rule of 11:** The provided integer is divisible if the difference between the sum of the digits at odd places and the sum of the digits at even places is 0 or divisible by 11.

**Calculation:**

8A5146B is divisible by 88

So, 8A5146B is divisible by 8 and 11

⇒ 46B should be divisible by 8

Put B = 4, 464 is divisible by 8

Hence, B = 4

Now, 8A51464 should be divisible by 11

⇒ (8 + 5 + 4 + 4) - (A + 1 + 6) should be divisible by 11

⇒ 21 - (A + 7) should be divisible by 11

⇒ 14 - A should be divisible by 11

Put A = 3 then, 14 - 3 = 11 which is divisible by 11

So, A = 3

Now, BA = 4³ = 64

**∴ The value of BA is 64**

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are (8x - 15)°,(6x - 11)° and ( 4x – 10)°. What is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The angles of a triangle are (8x - 15)°,(6x - 11)°, and ( 4x – 10)°

**Concept used:**

The sum of three angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculation:**

(8x - 15) + (6x - 11) + ( 4x – 10) = 180

⇒ 8x - 15 + 6x - 11 + 4x – 10 = 180

⇒ 18x - 36 = 180

⇒ 18x = 180 + 36 = 216

⇒ x = 216/18 = 12

**∴ The value of x is 12°**

questions.question: A journey of 900 km is completed in 11 h. If two-fifth of the journey is completed at the speed of 60 km/h, at what speed (in km/h) is the remaining journey completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The total time to cover 900 km = 11 h

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Time is taken to cover two-fifth of the journey = [(2/5) × 900]/60 = 360/60 = 6 h

The speed of the remaining distance = (900 - 360)/(11 - 6)

= 540/5 km/h

= 108 km/h

**∴ The speed of the remaining journey is 108 km/h**

questions.question: A and B are two prime numbers such that A > B and their LCM is 209. The value of A² - B is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The LCM of two prime numbers is simply their product.

⇒ A × B = 209

⇒ 209 = 19 × 11

Given A > B, we get A = 19 and B = 11.

⇒ A² − B = 19² − 11 = 361 − 11 = 350

**∴ The correct answer is 350.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A and B are prime numbers with A > B.

LCM(A, B) = 209

**Concept Used:**

The LCM of distinct prime numbers is exactly their product, as they do not share any common factors other than 1.

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM = A × B

⇒ A × B = 209

Factorising 209 into prime numbers:

⇒ 209 = 11 × 19

Since A and B are prime and A > B:

⇒ A = 19

⇒ B = 11

Substituting the values into the required expression A² − B:

⇒ A² − B = 19² − 11

⇒ A² − B = 361 − 11

⇒ A² − B = 350

**∴ The correct answer is 350.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM of Prime Numbers

The lowest common multiple (LCM) of distinct prime numbers is always their product. LCM(a, b) = a × b.

HCF of Prime Numbers

The highest common factor (HCF) of distinct prime numbers is always 1, as they have no other common divisors.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are co-prime if their HCF is 1. All prime numbers are co-prime to each other, and certain pairs of composite numbers can also be co-prime (e.g., 4 and 9).

questions.question: Aditya sells two wrist watches from his personal collection for ₹12,600 each. On the first watch, he gains 26% and, on the second, he loses 10%. Find the overall gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of each wristwatch = ₹12600

The profit on the first watch = 26%

The loss on the second watch = 10%

**Formula used:**

Cost price = (Selling price) × [100/(100 ± Profit%/Loss%)]

Profit% = Profit/(Cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Total selling price = 12600 × 2 = ₹25200

The cost price of two watches = 12600 × [100/(100 + 26)] + 12600 × [100/(100 - 10)]

= [12600 × (100/126)] + [12600 × (100/90)]

= 10000 + 14000

= ₹24000

The total profit = 25200 - 24000 = ₹1200

The gain percentage = (1200/24000) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The overall gain percentage is 5%**
